title: Headless published-content delivery for application consumers
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As an application developer, I want a minimal versioned JSON delivery contract for published Papyrus content, so that applications can consume articles without depending on a page renderer or internal CMS schema.

Definition of Done for later implementation: documented v1 contract, individual article retrieval, list/filter/pagination and public asset references, common visibility/update handling and isolation specifications. Structured fields plus a Markus body string are required; renderer-specific HTML or body IR is not a required interchange contract. Depends on the shared foundation; examine existing Published* and Markus/S3 projection before choosing static JSON versus request-time transport. Reuse M8 PPY-f293ea where appropriate; its latest/search JSON lacks the full article contract. No new publishing engine.

Deferred/YAGNI: Markdown+YAML export, exact Contentful API compatibility, extra export formats and authenticated draft previews. This is delivery for public application consumers, not an editorial API or a new authoring backend.

Approved post-save platform behavior: when headless delivery is enabled, publish, saved published edits and unpublish automatically refresh its outputs consistently with article/listings/indexes, sitemap and RSS/Atom. Private draft saves never enter public delivery. Ancillary failures must be visible/retryable. Detailed observable acceptance is in PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102. Implementation remains unstarted.

Organizing initiative: Markus for everything (PPY-23a743). This is one architecture with shared authored pages, includes/derived regeneration, published projection and delivery contracts. RSS/Atom and headless remain dependent on the shared foundation and post-save behavior. Incremental vertical slices are allowed as future planning, but a bespoke custom-Python composition shortcut contradicts the target design. Monitoring remains separate and linked, not a prerequisite. This architecture is now lower priority than the real Monitoring learning-loop slice; no implementation is authorized for it.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Planning delivery: branch develop, direct Kanbus-only commit/push per AGENTS.md; GitHub reports develop unprotected, so no PR is required. Verified all 22 new records by kbs show: types, permitted parent links, descriptions, Gherkin, open/unassigned state, provenance and dependency targets. Both delivery epics depend on the common published-content foundation. Full-board kbs validate remains at the same 15 pre-existing abbreviated dependency-target errors; no new validation errors. No code/tests/dependencies/infrastructure/deployment changes; behavior implementation and executable acceptance remain unstarted.
